blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Building a sustainable supply chain is no longer a communications project — it is an operational one. Customers and regulators are asking for real data: how much carbon, how much water, how much waste, how many fair-labour certifications. Vague claims are losing trust quickly.

The practical starting point is measurement. You cannot improve what you cannot measure, and most companies are still surprised by how hard it is to measure their own carbon footprint end-to-end. Once the numbers exist, the improvements become concrete: switch this lane from air to sea, consolidate those two warehouses, move that supplier to a certified one.

Sustainability at this level is slow, careful work, not a marketing campaign. But the companies that start early are the ones that, five years from now, will have answers when their biggest customers finally ask.

items.q: According to the text, sustainability in the supply chain has become mainly…
items.why: "is no longer a communications project — it is an operational one."

items.q: What does the text call the practical starting point?
items.why: "The practical starting point is measurement."

items.q: Why does the author say "you cannot improve what you cannot measure"?
options: Because regulators forbid changes without permits
Because measurement is cheaper than improvement
Because customers only trust certified suppliers
Because concrete change depends on having real numbers first
items.why: Inferência: sem os números, as melhorias (trocar a rota, consolidar armazéns) não têm base concreta.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Vague sustainability claims can quickly lose customer trust.
Companies that start early will have answers when customers ask.
A strong marketing campaign is enough to be genuinely sustainable.
Measuring your own carbon footprint is harder than most expect.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que sustentabilidade é trabalho operacional, não campanha de marketing.

items.q: What does the final paragraph suggest about companies that delay?
options: They will be fined immediately by regulators
They may lack real answers when big customers eventually demand data
They will save money in the short term and lose nothing
They will find measurement easier later on
items.why: Inferência: só quem começa cedo terá respostas quando os grandes clientes perguntarem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando o CEO sobre a medição da pegada de carbono. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before we announce anything publicly, I want to be honest with you about where we actually are. The disclosure deadline is next year, and right now we simply do not have reliable numbers for our full carbon footprint.

My advice is clear. We had better start measuring this quarter, not next year, because the data collection alone will take months once we include our suppliers. You should treat this as an operational project with a real owner, not something the communications team handles on the side.

I know the board would love a certification to put on the website. But a certificate without real data behind it is just a marketing campaign, and regulators can see through that very quickly. We ought to build the measurement first, then let the claims follow the numbers.

Once we have the footprint, the decisions get concrete. We can consolidate two of the warehouses, switch some freight from air to sea, and move a couple of suppliers to certified ones. But none of that is credible until we can show how we measured it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte want to do BEFORE announcing anything publicly?
options: Buy a certification for the website
Switch all freight from air to sea
Hand the project to the communications team
Be honest about where the company actually is
items.why: "before we announce anything publicly, I want to be honest with you about where we actually are."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say they had better start measuring this quarter?
options: Because data collection with suppliers will take months
Because the board demands it immediately
items.why: "the data collection alone will take months once we include our suppliers."

items.q: How does Charlotte describe a certificate without real data behind it?
items.why: "a certificate without real data behind it is just a marketing campaign."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about the board's wish for a certification?
options: It has already been approved by regulators
It is understandable but risky without the numbers to support it
It is the safest and fastest path to real sustainability
items.why: Inferência: ela reconhece o desejo ("would love"), mas avisa que reguladores percebem a falta de dados.

items.q: What is Charlotte's overall recommendation on sequencing?
options: Announce a certification now and measure later
Measure first and let the claims follow the numbers
Make the claims first, then find data to match them
items.why: "We ought to build the measurement first, then let the claims follow the numbers."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Sustainability is now an operational project." Here operational means…
options: related to the actual running of the business
items.why: Operational = operacional: ligado à execução real da operação, não à comunicação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Regulators no longer accept vague claims; they want ___ they can audit."
items.why: Real data = dados reais, o que os reguladores querem poder auditar.

items.q: "We must measure our carbon footprint end-to-end." A footprint here is…
options: the total environmental impact left by an activity
the size of the head office
items.why: Footprint = pegada: o impacto ambiental total deixado pela atividade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once the numbers exist, the plan becomes ___: switch this lane, consolidate that warehouse."
items.why: Concrete = concreto: específico e acionável, em oposição a vago.

items.q: "We will consolidate the two regional warehouses into one." To consolidate means to…
options: keep them exactly as they are
combine them into a single, stronger unit
items.why: Consolidate = consolidar: juntar em uma única unidade mais eficiente.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões sobre sustentabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO still has to sign off on the measurement plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new supplier standards across all regions." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two suppliers pushed back on the new certification requirement." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente recusar de vez.

items.q: "The team promised data by June but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A certificate alone will not move the needle on our real emissions." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
